answer.short: First event: rain. Branch probabilities: $0.35,0.65$; after $R$: $0.90,0.10$; after $\bar R$: $0.25,0.75$. Joint probabilities, top to bottom: $0.315,0.035,0.1625,0.4875$. $P(\text{Bus})=0.4775=47.75\%$.
answer.worked:
Let $R$ mean rain and $B$ mean taking the bus. Rain is the first event.
$$\begin{aligned}P(R)&=0.35\\P(\bar R)&=1-0.35=0.65\\P(B\mid R)&=0.90\\P(\bar B\mid R)&=1-0.90=0.10\\P(B\mid\bar R)&=0.25\\P(\bar B\mid\bar R)&=1-0.25=0.75\end{aligned}$$
Multiply along each path:
$$\begin{aligned}P(R\cap B)&=0.35\times0.90=0.315\\P(R\cap\bar B)&=0.35\times0.10=0.035\\P(\bar R\cap B)&=0.65\times0.25=0.1625\\P(\bar R\cap\bar B)&=0.65\times0.75=0.4875\\P(\text{Bus})&=0.315+0.1625\\P(\text{Bus})&=0.4775=47.75\%\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:

$$\begin{aligned}P(S)&=0.60\\P(\bar S)&=1-0.60=0.40\\P(\bar P\mid S)&=0.15\\P(P\mid S)&=1-0.15=0.85\\P(P\mid\bar S)&=0.40\\P(\bar P\mid\bar S)&=1-0.40=0.60\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{Pass})&=0.60\times0.85+0.40\times0.40\\P(\text{Pass})&=0.51+0.16\\P(\text{Pass})&=0.67=67\%\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
The second coin's result is independent of the first coin's result.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{second heads}\mid\text{first tails})&=P(\text{second heads})\\P(\text{second heads}\mid\text{first tails})&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
The second die's result is independent of the first die's result.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{second is 4}\mid\text{first is odd})&=P(\text{second is 4})\\P(\text{second is 4}\mid\text{first is odd})&=\frac{1}{6}\end{align*}$$
For multistage independent events, knowing that $B$ occurred does not change the probability of $A$, so $P(A\mid B)=P(A)$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}P(A)&=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B\mid A)}\\P(A)&=\frac{p}{1/4}\\P(A)&=4p\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(B)&=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(A\mid B)}\\P(B)&=\frac{p}{1/5}\\P(B)&=5p\end{align*}$$

The Venn diagram has $3p$ in $A$ only, $p$ in the intersection and $4p$ in $B$ only. Using the Venn diagram,

$$\begin{align*}P(A\cup B)&=3p+p+4p\\P(A\cup B)&=8p\\P(A'\cap B')&=1-8p.\end{align*}$$

For independence, $P(F)=P(F\mid S)$. Here,
$$\begin{aligned}P(F)&=\frac{3}{10},\\P(F\mid S)&=\frac18.\end{aligned}$$

entries.description: Conditional Probability

Conditional probability measures how likely one event will occur when we already know another event has happened.
Conditional probability only applies when two events are
• dependent (for multistage experiments)
• not mutually exclusive (for compound events).

Key phrases that signal conditional probability:
"If... then" - "If it's raining, then what's the probability of carrying an umbrella?"
"Given" - "Given that a student studies, what's the probability they pass?"
"Knowing that" - "Knowing that someone is tall, what's the probability they play basketball?"

entries.description: Conditional Probability for Independent/Mutually Exclusive Events

multistage independent events
P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B)
∴ P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B)
             = [P(A) × P(B)]/P(B)
             = P(A)
Knowing B happened doesn't change A's probability.
Similarly,
P(B|A) = P(B)

presentation.alignment: Centred formulae; successive derivation lines aligned at equals signs; explanatory prose left aligned.

entries.description:
mutually exclusive events
P(A ∩ B) = 0
∴ P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B)
             = 0
If B has occurred, A cannot happen at the same time.
Similarly,
P(B|A) = 0

presentation.alignment: Centred formulae; successive derivation lines aligned at equals signs; explanatory prose left aligned.
